text: Since year parameter get_holidays() accepts single value, can use purrr::map() get holidays multiple years. title: Introduction to holideh
text: 2027, Christmas Boxing Day fall Saturday Sunday, respectively. Therefore, observed proceeding Monday Tuesday. federal government setting, likely using observed dates, actual holiday dates: example gives overview helpers package:
code: simple_example <- tibble(   dates = seq(from = ymd("2027-12-20"), to = ymd("2028-01-05"), by = "1 day") )  simple_example #> # A tibble: 17 × 1 #>    dates      #>    <date>     #>  1 2027-12-20 #>  2 2027-12-21 #>  3 2027-12-22 #>  4 2027-12-23 #>  5 2027-12-24 #>  6 2027-12-25 #>  7 2027-12-26 #>  8 2027-12-27 #>  9 2027-12-28 #> 10 2027-12-29 #> 11 2027-12-30 #> 12 2027-12-31 #> 13 2028-01-01 #> 14 2028-01-02 #> 15 2028-01-03 #> 16 2028-01-04 #> 17 2028-01-05 holiday_dates <- pull(holidays, date) obs_dates <- pull(holidays, observed_date) simple_example <- simple_example %>%   mutate(     # `wday()` is from lubridate     day_of_week = wday(dates, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),          # Check if a date is a weekend     weekend = is_weekend(dates),          # Check if a holiday falls on a date using the "actual dates"     true_holiday = is_holiday(dates, holiday_dates),          # Check if a holiday falls on a date using the "observed dates"     obs_holiday = is_holiday(dates, obs_dates),          # Check if a date is a business day (i.e. not holiday + not weekend)     bizday = is_bizday(dates, holidays = obs_dates)   ) %>%   left_join(     select(holidays, observed_date, name_en),     by = c("dates" = "observed_date")   )  simple_example #> # A tibble: 17 × 7 #>    dates      day_of_week weekend true_holiday obs_holiday bizday name_en        #>    <date>     <ord>       <lgl>   <lgl>        <lgl>       <lgl>  <chr>          #>  1 2027-12-20 Monday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #>  2 2027-12-21 Tuesday     FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #>  3 2027-12-22 Wednesday   FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #>  4 2027-12-23 Thursday    FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #>  5 2027-12-24 Friday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #>  6 2027-12-25 Saturday    TRUE    TRUE         FALSE       FALSE  NA             #>  7 2027-12-26 Sunday      TRUE    TRUE         FALSE       FALSE  NA             #>  8 2027-12-27 Monday      FALSE   FALSE        TRUE        FALSE  Christmas Day  #>  9 2027-12-28 Tuesday     FALSE   FALSE        TRUE        FALSE  Boxing Day     #> 10 2027-12-29 Wednesday   FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #> 11 2027-12-30 Thursday    FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #> 12 2027-12-31 Friday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #> 13 2028-01-01 Saturday    TRUE    TRUE         FALSE       FALSE  NA             #> 14 2028-01-02 Sunday      TRUE    FALSE        FALSE       FALSE  NA             #> 15 2028-01-03 Monday      FALSE   FALSE        TRUE        FALSE  New Year's Day #> 16 2028-01-04 Tuesday     FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA             #> 17 2028-01-05 Wednesday   FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA

title: Introduction to holideh
text: Consider scenario calculate productivity number points accumulated reporting period divided number business days. addition, suppose points reported biweekly basis Wednesdays. , goal make use count_bizdays() function, counts number business days two dates (inclusively). data frame, need add start reporting period (13 days prior): Now start end dates, can calculate number business days reporting period. Note count_bizdays() vectorised start end, need wrap map2_int(). number business days, calculating productivity straightforward: can check work zooming period 2027-12-16 2027-12-29 making use helper functions previously demonstrated simple example. ✅ eight business days reporting period, matches results .
code: real_example <- tibble(   end = seq(from = ymd("2027-11-03"), to = ymd("2028-01-27"), by = "2 weeks"),   points = ceiling(runif(length(end), min = 90, max = 120)) )  real_example #> # A tibble: 7 × 2 #>   end        points #>   <date>      <dbl> #> 1 2027-11-03    103 #> 2 2027-11-17    111 #> 3 2027-12-01     95 #> 4 2027-12-15    117 #> 5 2027-12-29     94 #> 6 2028-01-12    120 #> 7 2028-01-26    109 real_example <- real_example %>%   mutate(start = end - days(13)) %>%   relocate(start)  real_example #> # A tibble: 7 × 3 #>   start      end        points #>   <date>     <date>      <dbl> #> 1 2027-10-21 2027-11-03    103 #> 2 2027-11-04 2027-11-17    111 #> 3 2027-11-18 2027-12-01     95 #> 4 2027-12-02 2027-12-15    117 #> 5 2027-12-16 2027-12-29     94 #> 6 2027-12-30 2028-01-12    120 #> 7 2028-01-13 2028-01-26    109 real_example <- real_example %>%   mutate(     n_bizdays = map2_int(       start, end,       \(from, to) count_bizdays(from, to, holidays = obs_dates)     ),     productivity = points / n_bizdays   )  real_example #> # A tibble: 7 × 5 #>   start      end        points n_bizdays productivity #>   <date>     <date>      <dbl>     <int>        <dbl> #> 1 2027-10-21 2027-11-03    103        10         10.3 #> 2 2027-11-04 2027-11-17    111         9         12.3 #> 3 2027-11-18 2027-12-01     95        10          9.5 #> 4 2027-12-02 2027-12-15    117        10         11.7 #> 5 2027-12-16 2027-12-29     94         8         11.8 #> 6 2027-12-30 2028-01-12    120         9         13.3 #> 7 2028-01-13 2028-01-26    109        10         10.9 tibble(   dates = seq(from = ymd("2027-12-16"), to = ymd("2027-12-29"), by = "1 day"),   day_of_week = wday(dates, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE) ) %>%   mutate(     # Check if a date is a weekend     weekend = is_weekend(dates),          # Check if a holiday falls on a date using the "actual dates"     true_holiday = is_holiday(dates, holiday_dates),          # Check if a holiday falls on a date using the "observed dates"     obs_holiday = is_holiday(dates, obs_dates),          # Check if a date is a business day (i.e. not holiday + not weekend)     bizday = is_bizday(dates, holidays = obs_dates)   ) %>%   left_join(     select(holidays, observed_date, name_en),     by = c("dates" = "observed_date")   ) #> # A tibble: 14 × 7 #>    dates      day_of_week weekend true_holiday obs_holiday bizday name_en       #>    <date>     <ord>       <lgl>   <lgl>        <lgl>       <lgl>  <chr>         #>  1 2027-12-16 Thursday    FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  2 2027-12-17 Friday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  3 2027-12-18 Saturday    TRUE    FALSE        FALSE       FALSE  NA            #>  4 2027-12-19 Sunday      TRUE    FALSE        FALSE       FALSE  NA            #>  5 2027-12-20 Monday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  6 2027-12-21 Tuesday     FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  7 2027-12-22 Wednesday   FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  8 2027-12-23 Thursday    FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #>  9 2027-12-24 Friday      FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA            #> 10 2027-12-25 Saturday    TRUE    TRUE         FALSE       FALSE  NA            #> 11 2027-12-26 Sunday      TRUE    TRUE         FALSE       FALSE  NA            #> 12 2027-12-27 Monday      FALSE   FALSE        TRUE        FALSE  Christmas Day #> 13 2027-12-28 Tuesday     FALSE   FALSE        TRUE        FALSE  Boxing Day    #> 14 2027-12-29 Wednesday   FALSE   FALSE        FALSE       TRUE   NA

title: Tools for Working with Canadian Dates
text: Consider following setup: 2027, Christmas (December 25) Boxing Day (December 26) fall Saturday Sunday, respectively. Therefore, observed Monday (December 27) Tuesday (December 28), respectively. holideh also contains additional helpers operations: is_weekend(): Given vector dates, detects whether supplied dates weekend (typically Saturday Sunday, can modified). is_holiday(): Given vector dates vector holiday dates, detects whether supplied dates holiday. , important consider whether analysis requires official holiday dates observed holiday dates. is_bizday(): Given vector dates vector holiday dates (optionally, vector considered “weekend”), detects whether supplied dates business day: is_weekend(), is_holiday(), is_bizday() predicate functions (functions return either TRUE FALSE), can also used within purrr::keep() purrr::discard(). detailed usages, see Get Started vignette.
code: holiday_date <- ymd(c("2027-12-25", "2027-12-26")) observed_date <- ymd(c("2027-12-27", "2027-12-28"))  calendar <- seq(from = ymd("2027-12-24"), to = ymd("2027-12-30"), by = "1 day") set_names(is_weekend(calendar), calendar) #> 2027-12-24 2027-12-25 2027-12-26 2027-12-27 2027-12-28 2027-12-29 2027-12-30  #>      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE set_names(is_holiday(calendar, holiday_date), calendar) #> 2027-12-24 2027-12-25 2027-12-26 2027-12-27 2027-12-28 2027-12-29 2027-12-30  #>      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE set_names(is_holiday(calendar, observed_date), calendar) #> 2027-12-24 2027-12-25 2027-12-26 2027-12-27 2027-12-28 2027-12-29 2027-12-30  #>      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE set_names(is_bizday(calendar, holiday_date), calendar) #> 2027-12-24 2027-12-25 2027-12-26 2027-12-27 2027-12-28 2027-12-29 2027-12-30  #>       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE set_names(is_bizday(calendar, observed_date), calendar) #> 2027-12-24 2027-12-25 2027-12-26 2027-12-27 2027-12-28 2027-12-29 2027-12-30  #>       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE

text: tibble columns: date <date> date holiday occurs. observed_date <date> date holiday observed (celebrated). example, Christmas Day falls Sunday, observed (celebrated) proceeding Monday. name_en <chr> name holiday, English. name_fr <chr> name holiday, French. federal <lgl> Whether holiday federal holiday. holiday_id <int> id holiday. provinces <list> list tibbles containing information provinces observing holiday source links.

text: Holiday dates can obtained using get_holidays(), get_province(), defining custom vector holidays.

title: Detect non-business days — off_day
code: library(lubridate)  dates <- seq.Date(from = ymd("2025-12-20"), to = ymd("2025-12-31"), by = "1 day") winter_holidays <- ymd(c("2025-12-25", "2025-12-26"))  rlang::set_names(is_holiday(dates, holidays = winter_holidays), dates) #> 2025-12-20 2025-12-21 2025-12-22 2025-12-23 2025-12-24 2025-12-25 2025-12-26  #>      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE       TRUE       TRUE  #> 2025-12-27 2025-12-28 2025-12-29 2025-12-30 2025-12-31  #>      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE  rlang::set_names(is_weekend(dates), dates) #> 2025-12-20 2025-12-21 2025-12-22 2025-12-23 2025-12-24 2025-12-25 2025-12-26  #>       TRUE       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE  #> 2025-12-27 2025-12-28 2025-12-29 2025-12-30 2025-12-31  #>       TRUE       TRUE      FALSE      FALSE      FALSE
